questions.q: Why does this capstone import only nine specific tables instead of the whole AdventureWorksDW2014 database?
options: The written scope from Lesson 84 defines exactly which tables are needed — a smaller, deliberate model is easier to reason about at every later step
SQL Server only allows nine tables to be imported at a time
Power BI Desktop has a hard limit of nine tables per file
Importing more tables is always faster regardless of need
questions.explain: This mirrors Chapter 4's star-schema discipline: import exactly what the scoped requirements need, not everything available, so the model stays easy to reason about.

questions.q: Why was Import mode chosen for this capstone rather than DirectQuery?
options: The project doesn't need real-time data, and Import gives the fastest report-building experience while actively designing visuals
DirectQuery is not supported for SQL Server at all
Import mode is always the only available option
DirectQuery requires a Premium license that this project doesn't have
questions.explain: The choice is deliberate and scope-driven: since Lesson 84's requirements never called for real-time data, Import mode's build-speed advantage wins for this project.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend importing some columns you're not immediately sure you'll need?
options: Columns often turn out useful once building actual visuals, and removing unused ones later (in Power Query) is cheap — reconnecting later to add a missed column is not
Power BI requires importing every column in a table with no exceptions
Unused columns automatically improve refresh performance
It's impossible to add a column back later without starting over
questions.explain: The asymmetry matters: cutting an unneeded column later in Power Query (Lesson 86) is trivial, but discovering mid-build that a needed column was never imported means going back to the source connection.

questions.q: What is one recommended sanity check right after loading the tables?
options: Confirm row counts look plausible for each table and that no table loaded completely empty
Confirm every column name is in alphabetical order
Confirm the file size is under 1 MB
Confirm all tables have exactly the same number of rows
questions.explain: Plausible row counts (DimDate spanning years, FactInternetSales in the tens of thousands) and no unexpectedly empty tables are the quick checks before moving into cleanup.

questions.q: Why are DimCustomer and DimReseller included in the import list, even though Lesson 84's requirements didn't mention them directly?
options: They're needed to relate FactInternetSales and FactResellerSales to territory data
They contain the DAX measures needed for the project
They were included by mistake and should be removed
They're required for Power BI Desktop to even open the file
questions.explain: The relationship path to DimSalesTerritory runs through DimCustomer (for internet sales) and DimReseller (for reseller sales) — necessary supporting tables, even though the requirement itself is about territory, not customers or resellers directly.
